Halcyra Airways' engine on WO-2618 loses its 36 segments until 6 Dec against an 8 Nov induction, moving redelivery 12 days at USD 9K per day. Takamori and Cascadia are approved for the segment but quote 84 and 90 days, so they can rescue the 2027 line, not WO-2618 directly.

Re-sequencing alone is USD 4.5K cheaper but still moves Halcyra 5 days and depends on the shop compressing the LPT build. qa.answer: Four options. Split the 2027 seal ring line 60/40 to Takamori and Cascadia and have Lindqvist ship WO-2618 first after the rebuild (USD 49.5K, no redelivery slip, recommended), split the 2027 line only and accept the slip (USD 124K including 12 days of LDs), re-sequence WO-2618 so the LPT module builds last (USD 45K, 5 day slip), or accept Lindqvist's dates (USD 108K in LDs, 12 day slip).

Re-sequencing is the cheapest at USD 45K, all of it 5 days of expected LDs at USD 9K per day. The recommended option costs USD 49.5K: USD 22.5K of Takamori and Cascadia price premium on 51 segments and USD 33.5K of air freight, less USD 6.4K saved by moving the fuel nozzles to Laem Chabang. It is the cheapest option that holds the 19 Jan redelivery.

In 2024 a US mill cut nickel superalloy allocation by 35% and we split 60/40 to Takamori Precision Castings at an 8% premium (PRE-05), which held the engine inductions. Takamori's seal ring price is again 8% over the incumbent. The lesson was to lock second-source slots the same week the notice lands, because they sell out within 10 days.

WO-2618 needs 36 LPT seal ring segments at induction on 8 Nov. With furnace 3 down for six weeks, Lindqvist re-confirmed them for 6 Dec, a 28 day slip against 16 days of work-order float, so Halcyra Airways' redelivery moves 12 days to 31 Jan. Takamori and Cascadia quote 84 and 90 days, landing 30 Dec and 5 Jan, so moving WO-2618 itself to them would make it worse.
